title: Adopt Centralized Agentic MAPE-K for the SWIM Demonstrator
context: SWIM-SASS-001 concerns the SWIM Self-Adaptive Web System, a research demonstrator combining LLM-supported architecture design with Agentic-AI-supported runtime adaptation. SWIM must process incoming web requests with basic and optional processing, dynamically adjust server allocation and optional-content dimming, and observe response time, workload, utilization, server state, and dimmer state. Adaptation seeks average response time at or below 0.75 seconds while preserving optional functionality and avoiding unnecessary resources. Workload changes, delayed server activation, incomplete observations, and incorrect LLM reasoning introduce uncertainty. Three architectures were evaluated using architect-defined quality-attribute weights and architectural validation. All received architectural-level PASS verdicts; these are not evidence of deployment readiness or guaranteed response-time attainment. Numerical decision support recommended A3, while prototype-alignment decision support recommended A1. The human architect subsequently approved A1. This ADR records that final decision, superseding the earlier recommendation-stage pending approval status without changing the supplied scores or treating unresolved operating parameters as approved.
decision_drivers: FR1 and FR2: Process incoming web requests while retaining distinct basic and optional processing.
FR3 and FR4: Dynamically scale servers and adjust the optional-content dimmer through approved SWIM effectors.
FR5: Observe average response time, workload, server utilization, server state, and dimmer state, including pending activation and incomplete observations.
AG1 and performance: Maintain average response time at or below 0.75 seconds under workload variation; priority very_high, weight 0.30.
Scalability: Adapt computing capacity within the trusted one-to-six-server range; priority high, weight 0.20.
Reliability: Maintain dependable adaptation and recover from unsuccessful or unsettled changes; priority high, weight 0.15.
AG4 and safety: Prevent unsafe or policy-violating proposals from reaching effectors through mandatory deterministic validation and no direct LLM effector access; priority high, weight 0.15.
AG3 and resource efficiency: Remove unnecessary capacity when workload decreases; priority medium, weight 0.10.
Explainability: Preserve understandable, evidence-linked architectural and runtime rationale; priority medium, weight 0.10.
AG2: Preserve or restore optional functionality when response-time headroom permits, coordinating quality restoration with resource allocation.
Include design-time LLM support, architectural RAG, runtime agentic control, deterministic safety enforcement, adaptation memory, and human oversight.

Prefer strong traceability between the approved architecture and the implemented, experimentally demonstrated centralized SWIM prototype, while distinguishing structural alignment from verification of every design detail.

Use deterministic weighted scoring on the supplied 1-to-5 scale as transparent decision support only. The weights are architect-defined demonstrator inputs, not universally optimal values; final architecture authority remains with the human architect.

alternatives_considered.name: Centralized Agentic MAPE-K
key_strengths: One logical controller coordinates server scaling and dimming using a shared runtime snapshot.
A single inspectable deterministic execution boundary supports safety auditing and per-action validation.
A centralized episode history connects observations, retrieval, rationale, safety verdicts, execution, and measured outcomes.
Most closely matches the demonstrated centralized SWIM runtime prototype and was the prototype-alignment recommendation.
Quality-attribute scores: performance 3, scalability 4, reliability 3, safety 5, resource efficiency 4, explainability 5; weighted rank 2.
All eight deterministic architectural checks passed, LLM requirement validation passed overall, and final architectural validation was PASS.
key_weaknesses: LLM reasoning remains on the adaptation path; no independent fast dimmer loop mitigates slow planning.
The logical controller is an adaptation dependency and potential latency bottleneck.
Observation freshness, pending capacity, action sequencing, and recovery must be coordinated in one control path.
Architectural validation retained partial coverage for demonstrated response-time attainment, workload responsiveness, bounded recovery, and centralized-controller reliability.

alternatives_considered.name: Coordinating Peer Adaptation Agents
key_strengths: Specialized capacity and optional-content agents can analyze independently and use focused retrieval.
Explicit peer coordination makes conflicting proposals visible.
Transactional reservations, ordered commits, common policy versions, and gateway fencing address jointly unsafe actions.
Quality-attribute scores: performance 3, scalability 4, reliability 3, safety 4, resource efficiency 3, explainability 4; weighted rank 3.
All eight deterministic architectural checks passed, LLM requirement validation passed overall, and final architectural validation was PASS.
key_weaknesses: Negotiation and coordinated commits add latency and consistency obligations; authoritative coordination remains necessary for execution.
Federated memories complicate explanation and attribution of joint outcomes.
The bounded six-server deployment does not establish a need for distributed planning, and the centralized prototype does not demonstrate the required peer protocol.
Response-time attainment, optional-quality balancing, precise dimmer-step semantics, incomplete-observation handling, and time-bounded recovery require further specification or evidence.

alternatives_considered.name: Two-Timescale Supervisory Adaptation
key_strengths: An independent deterministic dimmer loop removes LLM latency from immediate dimmer adaptation.
Fast dimming can mitigate transient pressure while supervisory server additions become active.
Preapproved dimmer behavior can continue during supervisory LLM unavailability, subject to fresh observations and the shared safety boundary.
All six quality attributes scored 4; weighted rank 1 and numerical recommendation.
All eight deterministic architectural checks passed, LLM requirement validation passed overall, and final architectural validation was PASS.
key_weaknesses: Requires additional implementation and validation of loop timing, arbitration, hysteresis, and cross-timescale outcome attribution.
Fast dimming may mask sustained capacity shortages; quality restoration and scale-in may interact to produce oscillation.
The independent fast loop and its interaction mechanisms are not established by the supplied centralized prototype evidence.
Architectural PASS does not demonstrate response-time attainment; shared monitoring, arbitration, and execution remain critical dependencies.

decision.architect_rationale: A1 is selected because it provides the closest structural alignment with the implemented and experimentally demonstrated runtime prototype. Although A3 achieved the highest weighted trade-off score, A1 already realizes the required centralized agentic adaptation loop, runtime RAG, LLM-supported analysis and planning, deterministic safety validation, approved SWIM effectors, post-execution validation, runtime memory, bounded recovery, and human escalation. Selecting A1 therefore provides stronger traceability between the approved design and the implemented demonstrator, while A3 remains a promising future architectural extension.
decision.why_not_highest_ranked_if_applicable: A3 is the numerical winner at 4.00, ahead of A1 at 3.80 and A2 at 3.45. Totals are deterministic sums of architect-defined weights multiplied by supplied architectural assessment scores. Relative to A1, A3 gains 0.30 for performance and 0.15 for reliability, while A1 gains 0.15 for safety and 0.10 for explainability; equal scalability and resource-efficiency scores leave A3 ahead by 0.20. These are advisory assessments, not measured comparative runtime results. The architect selected A1 for prototype alignment and design-to-implementation traceability rather than numerical rank. No scores or weights were changed to justify that choice. Numerical ranking was decision support only; final authority remained with the human architect, and approval was not automatic.

approved_architecture_summary: A1 uses one logical centralized MAPE-K controller with an untrusted LLM analyzer and planner, a shared versioned runtime snapshot, centralized adaptation memory, and a deterministic execution boundary. The controller coordinates SWIM server scaling and optional-content dimming. Only validated actions reach approved effectors; observed outcomes, not LLM assertions or effector acknowledgments, determine adaptation results. Design-time architectural RAG and LLM reasoning support human review without acquiring policy or deployment authority. The approved design does not include A2 peer coordination or A3's independent fast dimmer loop.
design_time_architecture: Requirements and Trusted Policy Registry / Maintain supplied requirements and machine-readable trusted constraints independently of generated reasoning; distinguish mandatory constraints from proposed operating settings.
Architectural RAG / Retrieve architectural knowledge with identifiers and selection context before LLM reasoning; retrieved material remains advisory rather than executable policy.
LLM Architecture Reasoner / Generate and explain alternatives, including coordination, server startup delays, and safety limitations, using requirements and retrieved evidence.

Trade-off and Rationale Workspace / Preserve qualitative trade-offs, evidence links, and architect-defined weights. The candidate-generation stage does not itself select an architecture; subsequent supplied evaluation and human approval provide the decision recorded here.

Architect Review and Configuration Approval / Retain human authority over architecture, executable policies, and trusted-constraint changes. Architecture approval is recorded; unresolved retry, timing, freshness, dimmer-step interpretation, and anti-oscillation settings still require explicit configuration review.
runtime_architecture: SWIM Managed Web System / Process incoming requests with basic and optional work, and expose approved server and dimmer effectors only behind the protected execution interface.
Runtime Monitor and Snapshot Store / Collect all FR5 observations with timestamps, state versions, and missing-data indicators; distinguish active servers from pending activation.

Central Agentic Analyzer and Planner / Use current observations and retrieved experience to diagnose adaptation needs and propose coordinated actions with rationale, expected effects, and preconditions.

Adaptation Memory and Runtime Retrieval / Store and retrieve episodes containing observations, evidence, proposals, policy versions, safety verdicts, acknowledgments, and measured outcomes; experience never overrides trusted policy.
Deterministic Safety Gate and Execution Coordinator / Validate structured proposals against trusted policy and current state, serialize mutations, and reject stale, ambiguous, or conflicting actions.

Approved Effector Adapter / Connect validated add_server, remove_server, set_dimmer, and none decisions to approved SWIM interfaces; track acknowledgments and pending transitions without treating them as adaptation success.

Outcome Evaluator and Recovery Supervisor / Compare observed effects with intended effects and the 0.75-second target, record outcome evidence, coordinate bounded replanning, and escalate unresolved conditions. Prototype escalation is simulated, not a demonstrated production notification service.
runtime_control_flow: Monitor SWIM and build a timestamped, versioned snapshot containing average response time, workload, utilization, server state, and dimmer state, including missing data and pending transitions.

Retrieve relevant centralized adaptation episodes using workload, utilization, server-transition state, and dimmer context. Current observations and trusted policy take precedence over retrieved experience.

Diagnose response-time pressure and propose allowed actions. Coordinate dimmer reduction with delayed server activation; consider optional-content restoration and server removal when observed headroom permits.
Validate the structured proposal deterministically. Revalidate every state-changing action against the latest state before dispatch; a multi-action plan is not authorized wholesale.
Dispatch validated actions through the approved adapter to SWIM and observe their transitions. Requested capacity is not active capacity, and acknowledgment is not proof of successful adaptation.

Evaluate actual effects over an architect-approved observation window. Record PASS only when the intended effect is observed and the response-time target is met, PARTIAL for incomplete improvement, and FAIL for execution failure or unsuccessful settled outcomes. Keep incomplete or unsettled evidence pending.
Store observations, rationale, retrieval evidence, policy version, safety verdicts, execution records, and measured outcomes in adaptation memory.

For rejected or unsuccessful proposals, refresh observations and replan within the approved recovery policy, repeating safety validation. Two revised proposals after the initial proposal are proposed, not established here as an approved exact retry setting.

On exhausted recovery, planner unavailability, or insufficient observations, dispatch no unvalidated mutation, continue monitoring, and escalate with the evidence trail. Do not mistake a starting server for failed capacity. Holding state does not guarantee response-time compliance; the demonstrator's escalation event remains explicitly simulated.
safety_boundaries: The LLM has neither effector credentials nor a direct invocation path. Only the deterministic gate and approved adapter can authorize and dispatch runtime changes.
Allowed runtime actions are exactly add_server, remove_server, set_dimmer, and none. Unknown, malformed, or ambiguous proposals must not authorize mutations.
Enforce server bounds of 1 through 6 while accounting for active servers, reserved additions, and pending removals; never remove the last serving server.

Enforce dimmer bounds of 0.0 through 1.0 and the trusted 0.25 step. Precise permitted-value and transition semantics require approved clarification without weakening the supplied constraint; reject ambiguous proposals.
Require sufficiently complete, fresh observations and matching state versions for state-dependent actions; serialize changes and revalidate each mutation before dispatch.
The 0.75-second response-time target remains immutable trusted configuration. Structural safety validation cannot guarantee future performance under uncertain workload.
Architectural RAG, runtime memory, and generated rationale are advisory. They cannot modify trusted constraints, authorize effectors, or replace human design-time approval.
Architectural acceptance does not imply that all operating parameters, implementation protections, or production deployment conditions have been validated.
positive_consequences: The approved architecture aligns closely with the demonstrated SWIM controller, strengthening research traceability without introducing unestablished peer or fast-loop mechanisms.
One logical decision point simplifies coordination of delayed capacity changes and optional-content control.
A single protected execution boundary provides an inspectable location for deterministic policy enforcement.
Centralized episodes support understandable end-to-end explanations and contextual reuse of successful, partial, failed, and unsettled adaptations.
Explicit post-execution evaluation distinguishes proposals and acknowledgments from observed adaptation results.
Joint consideration of utilization, optional quality, and pending capacity can support avoiding redundant scale-out and identifying scale-in opportunities.
negative_consequences: A1 accepts lower assessed performance and reliability support than A3, retaining LLM-dependent adaptation latency and no independent fast response loop.
Failure or delay in the centralized controller can suspend adaptation even when SWIM continues serving requests.
Safety-preserving withholding of mutations may leave response-time violations unresolved.
Centralization concentrates responsibility for observation freshness, serialization, pending transitions, and recovery in one control path.
The decision does not provide the prospective responsiveness benefits of A3; adding those mechanisms would be a future architectural extension requiring review.
Implementation alignment does not remove the need for operating-policy approval, fault handling, workload testing, and production escalation design.
risks: Rapid workload changes or slow LLM inference may make proposals stale before execution and repeatedly delay mitigation.
Response time may exceed 0.75 seconds even with six servers and minimum optional content; the system must expose and escalate infeasibility rather than promise success.
Incomplete observations, incorrect pending-capacity accounting, or races between validation and dispatch may undermine intended enforcement.
Structurally valid proposals may still worsen performance, retain excess capacity, or suppress optional functionality unnecessarily.
Poor retrieval relevance, obsolete policy context, or misattributed outcomes may reinforce ineffective adaptations and cause oscillation.
Uncertain effector completion, unsafe server removal, or controller restart may cause duplicate actions or inconsistent state unless reconciled.
Attempt-count limits alone may allow unbounded elapsed recovery through indefinite pending states or repeated episode-budget resets.
Simulated operator escalation may be mistaken for operational human oversight unless its limitations remain explicit.
remaining_validation_needs: Validate representative SWIM workloads and timing against the 0.75-second target, defining the response-time averaging window, workload envelope, LLM latency measurements, burst scenarios, activation delays, observation lag, and saturation behavior. No supplied comparative runtime results establish A1 or A3 performance superiority.
Confirm preservation of required basic processing during dimmer reduction and quantify optional-content restoration and resource allocation behavior.
Approve observation sampling, per-action completeness and freshness criteria, state-version rules, settling windows, startup deadlines, and maximum pending durations.
Specify and test the exact trusted 0.25 dimmer-step interpretation, server boundary behavior, pending reservations, fail-closed parsing, and policy integrity.

Verify every actual execution path is non-bypassable, including deployment permissions, recovery, and operator intervention. Test serialization and fresh-state checks through dispatch rather than assuming prototype alignment proves them.
Specify and fault-test safe server draining, effector idempotency, lost acknowledgments, uncertain completion, partial multi-action execution, controller restart, and state reconciliation.
Approve exact retry budgets, planner and effector deadlines, episode identity, budget-reset rules, and escalation timing so recovery is bounded in elapsed time as well as attempts.
Define and test hysteresis, cooldowns, quality-restoration criteria, and scale-in ordering to avoid oscillation, prolonged optional-content suppression, and unnecessary capacity.
Test centralized-controller failure and planner unavailability without assuming that bounded retries establish availability or a fast fallback path.
Verify runtime outcome classifications and ensure unsettled effects remain pending rather than being promoted to PASS from acknowledgments alone.

Review retrieval provenance, relevance thresholds, retention, obsolete-policy handling, and evidence-to-rationale traceability. A1 references AK1, AK2, AK4, AK5, AK6, AK7, AK8, AK10, AK11, AK12, AK13, and AK15, but their contents were not supplied for independent verification.

Retain the complete alternatives, trade-off evaluation, and this human-approved ADR as design-time evidence. The current record supplies alternatives and rationale, but earlier capability-level validation does not independently prove actual RAG grounding or every design-time implementation capability.

Define real operational escalation recipients, delivery, acknowledgment, deadlines, operator procedures, and safe resumption before claiming production human notification. The demonstrated prototype provides simulated escalation only.

Keep architectural PASS, human architecture acceptance, and operational acceptance distinct. All alternatives passed structural and overall requirement review, with partial specifications and evidence gaps; this ADR does not convert those verdicts into deployment approval.
